main_text.p: Ex consonis quædam appellantur labiales, eò quòd adminiculo labiorum pronuntientur, ut sunt בּוּמָף bumâph.
Quædam dentales, ut sunt זַסְשָׁרָץ zas-scharáz.
Quædam linguales, ut sunt דַּטְלָנָת dat-lanáth.
Quædā palatales, ut sunt גִּיכָק gichák.
Quædā gutturales, ut sùt אַהְחָץ achág.

Quædam vocantur אֶהְוִי ehevi, quiescentes, quòd scilicet quiescant, hoc est, puncto carentes post longas vocales, & duas breves - pathah & ֶ segol, non legantur: ut, קָרְאָת karátha. גְּלָה gelé: לוֹ ló: צָדֶה zadé: פְּלָא pélé. Attamen in fine, ו vau sæpe sonat tanquam u, & י jod post ־ came-pathah, ִ holem, ֵ schurec, sonat tanquam i & utrunq; coalescit cum precedente vocali in diphthongum: ut, שָׁלוֹ schaléu, פִּיו piu, קָו káu, צָו záu, פָּנַי panái, אֱלִי

The "&" signs are printed ampersands; the Hebrew words are partly uncertain where vowel points overlap. The word "scharáz" is hyphenated across lines as printed ("zas-" / "scharáz"). Doubtful: the vowel points on the Hebrew forms and the exact placement of the Hebrew at the line ends.
